how.title: How it works
how.body: A family member photographs every strip, box and prescription. Six steps later the family has one clinician-checked list and a passport to carry to every doctor visit.

s1.title: Photograph
s1.body: Every strip, box and prescription in the house, cut strips included.

s2.title: Read
s2.body: A vision model turns photos into typed items: brand, strength, expiry, confidence.

s3.title: Match
s3.body: Each Bangladeshi brand maps to its generic. Unknown brands are searched on Bangladeshi medicine sites and marked unverified.

s4.title: Check
s4.body: A deterministic engine flags duplicates, same-class pairs, interactions, Beers 65+ drugs and expired strips.

s5.title: Confirm
s5.body: A pharmacist or doctor confirms or dismisses each finding, with a note, in under 30 seconds.

s6.title: Understand
s6.body: The family sees only confirmed findings in plain Bangla, a weekly report and a printable passport.

safe.title: AI for perception. Rules and humans for judgement.
safe.accent: এআই পড়ে, নিয়ম আর মানুষ বিচার করে।
safe.body: A vision model is good at reading a cut strip under a tube light. It is not who should decide that a 68-year-old is taking paracetamol twice. So it doesn’t.

r1.title: Rules make every finding.
r1.body: A deterministic engine flags duplicates, interactions, drugs risky after 65 and expired strips. Language models never create, remove or grade a finding.

r2.title: A clinician confirms before the family sees it.
r2.body: Findings start as pending. The API only ever returns confirmed findings to the family, and a test enforces it.

r3.title: We never tell anyone to stop a medicine.
r3.body: Explanations are checked for doses and stop-words, and always end: ডাক্তারের সাথে কথা না বলে কোনো ওষুধ বন্ধ বা পরিবর্তন করবেন না।

r4.title: Uncertain readings are marked.
r4.body: Anything read with under 75% confidence, or matched from the web, is shown as needing a human check.

r5.title: Names stay out of models.
r5.body: Only medicine photos and medicine names reach a model. Patient names and phone numbers never do.

r6.title: Photos are not kept.
r6.body: Photos are read in memory and discarded; the family sees a thumbnail once.

docs.title: OushodhSathi, in depth
docs.accent: ওষুধসাথী — পিচ, হোয়াইটপেপার ও সিস্টেম ড্যাশবোর্ড
docs.intro: The live pitch, technical whitepaper and system dashboard for the International AI Builders Congress 2026 (HealthSphere AI → ChronicCare AI). Every number on this page is either cited, read live from the running system, or labelled as demo data.

problem.body: An elderly patient with high blood pressure or diabetes in Bangladesh often collects medicines from three places: a hospital outpatient doctor, a village doctor, and the local drug shop. Each sees only their own prescription. The same molecule is sold under many brand names, so a family cannot tell that Napa and Ace are both paracetamol, or that two doctors have each started amlodipine.
problem.l1: Hypertension is now the most common illness in Bangladesh, at 78.28 per 1,000 people (BBS Health and Morbidity Status Survey 2025, as reported by <bss>BSS</bss> and <ds>The Daily Star</ds>).
problem.l2: Only 11% of people with hypertension had their blood pressure controlled below 140/90, a background figure in the <heart>WHO-HEARTS evaluation in Bangladesh (Heart, 2024)</heart>.
problem.l3: In a small 2011 study of 35 geriatric outpatients at a private hospital, 69% were prescribed five or more medicines (<trend>Trends of prescribing for out-door geriatric patients</trend>).

solution.body: A family member photographs every strip, box and prescription. A vision model reads the photos into a typed list; each brand is mapped to its generic; a deterministic rules engine flags duplicates, same-class pairs, interactions, drugs risky after 65 (AGS Beers Criteria), a high anticholinergic burden, look-alike names, the "triple whammy" (ACE inhibitor or ARB + diuretic + NSAID), medicines that need care at the latest kidney test (eGFR, CKD-EPI 2021), a kidney test that is due, antibiotics without a prescription (WHO AWaRe) and expired strips; a pharmacist or doctor confirms every flag; and only then does the family see a plain-Bangla explanation, a weekly report and a printable medicine passport with a QR code.

ai.body: One router (backend/app/llm_router.py) talks to every model through OpenAI-compatible APIs, falls through on 429, 5xx and timeouts, and caches every response in SQLite by a SHA-256 of task, model and messages. The shelf agent is built with Pydantic-AI and may call three tools: match_brand, lookup_unknown_brand and a read-only check_medicines. It cannot write flags.

r1.model: NVIDIA API Nemotron VL first; then free OpenRouter vision models (tested before use), NARAROUTER → EXPLAB → AGENTROUTER
r1.why: Cut strips, glare and Bangla text need a vision model; free models keep it affordable
r1.guard: Typed Pydantic output, one retry, then needs-review; confidence < 0.75 always shown for a human check

r2.model: Tavily search on medex.com.bd, arogga.com, medeasy.health + text model; Perplexity Agent API fallback
r2.why: Bangladesh has tens of thousands of brands; the seed table cannot hold them all
r2.guard: Model must cite a numbered result; stored as web_unverified with the source URL; failures never cached

r3.model: Ollama qwen2.5:3b locally first, cloud fallback
r3.why: Private and free when run locally
r3.guard: Only for confirmed flags; dose and stop-word filter; fixed template fallback; fixed safety sentence

r4.model: No model. Deterministic rules in backend/app/rules.py
r4.why: Judgement must be repeatable and auditable
r4.guard: Pure functions with tests; a clinician confirms every flag

ai.prompts: Prompts are versioned files in backend/app/prompts/ (extract_strip.v1, brand_lookup.v1, explain_bn.v1). Changing a prompt means a new version file and a new eval run.

safety.s1: Safety flags come only from the deterministic rules engine. Models never create, remove or change the severity of a flag.
safety.s2: Flags start as pending review. The family view of the API returns only confirmed flags, and a test enforces it.
safety.s3: No text tells a patient to stop, start or change a medicine or a dose.
safety.s4: Readings below 0.75 confidence and web-found brand matches are always marked for human confirmation.
safety.s5: Patient names and phone numbers are never sent to a model, only medicine photos and medicine names.
safety.s6: Photos are processed in memory and not stored after extraction.
safety.pdpo: These follow the data-minimisation and purpose-limitation principles of Bangladesh’s Personal Data Protection Ordinance 2025 (PDPO). OushodhSathi is a research prototype, not a medical device, and makes no compliance claim.
safety.fhir: The confirmed list exports as a FHIR R4 Bundle (a Patient with no identifiers beyond an internal id, and one MedicationStatement per medicine), ready for Bangladesh's Shared Health Record and health ID plans.

evaluation.intro: Extraction accuracy on our own labelled photos of real Bangladeshi strips (cut strips, Bangla text, blur):
evaluation.tests: The rules engine, API safety gate, router fallback and explanation guard are covered by the pytest suite; the live count is in the status table below.
evaluation.pilotIntro: What we find in real homes, reported as proportions with 95% Wilson score intervals, which stay honest at small sample sizes:
evaluation.sathiIntro: 80 test questions in Bangla, Banglish and English: app questions must be answered from the right guide entry; medical questions must go to the pharmacist; emergencies must get the 999 message; attempts to talk Sathi out of its rules must fail. The run fails, in CI too, if a single medical or emergency question gets an app answer.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: OushodhSathi helps a family check the medicines of an older relative. This notice says, in plain words, what we keep, who can see it and what you can do about it.

p: About the person: a name, age, district and long-term conditions you choose to enter.
Their medicine list, the findings a pharmacist or doctor confirmed, blood pressure readings, allergies, an emergency contact if you add one, and questions you send to the pharmacist.
Your email address, only if you give it, and whether you want our emails.
When you accepted this notice, and a short activity log (for example "3 medicines scanned") without names.
Photos of strips, boxes and prescriptions are read in memory and then discarded. Nothing is stored on our server. A strip photo can come back once as a small picture that stays only in your browser.
Before photographing a prescription, please fold or cover the patient's name.
To read the photos and look up unknown brands, we send medicine photos and medicine names to an AI provider. We never send the patient's name or any phone number to an AI model.
On the pilot, photos only go to providers that do not keep them.

If you hold the microphone button in Sathi, your recording goes to NVIDIA's speech service (Whisper large-v3) to be turned into text. We do not store or log the recording. The text appears in the box for you to read and correct before anything is sent.
Speech can contain names. Patient names are removed from the text before any AI model sees a question.

If you turn on the daily call in Settings, we record who agreed and when, the time you chose, and each call's answers (taken, not taken, or 9 for an emergency). Answers are saved as medicine ticks for the pharmacist.

When a real phone service is switched on, the mobile number is stored encrypted and is shared only with that phone-call provider, never with an AI model. Until then the call runs only as a simulator in your browser and no number is collected.
No calls between 21:00 and 08:00. You can stop the calls any time in Settings; the number is deleted at once. Calls are included in your data export and removed when you delete the household.
Anyone who has the private family link. Share it only with family; you can make a new link at any time in Settings, and the old one stops working.
The pharmacists and doctors who review the list, each with a personal login that records every decision they make.
A small number of OushodhSathi team members, only to help when you ask (for example a lost link).
The service runs on Render and the data is kept in a Supabase Postgres database, both in Singapore, the closest region to Bangladesh. Emails, if you want them, are sent through Resend.
In Settings you can turn emails on or off, make a new private link, download all the household's data, and delete the household. Deleting removes everything about it and cannot be undone.
If you no longer have a phone that opens the list, contact us and we will help.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms apply to the OushodhSathi pilot. Please read them before creating a list.

p: A medicine-checking service. Photos are read by AI, a fixed set of rules finds possible problems, and a registered pharmacist or doctor confirms each finding before the family sees it.
It is a pilot service, not a medical device, and not a replacement for the patient's own doctor.
It never tells anyone to stop, start or change a medicine or a dose. Decisions about treatment belong to the patient and their doctor. Talk to the doctor before changing anything.
It is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 999.
Create a list only for someone whose medicines you look after, with their agreement.
Keep the private family link safe and share it only with family.
Check the medicine list before sending it for review: you know the shelf best.
During the pilot the service is free for families. Features may change, and the pilot may end; if it does, we will tell you in advance so you can download your data.
We do our best to keep the service running and correct, but findings can be incomplete: a medicine that was not photographed, or a brand we do not know yet, cannot be checked.

contact.noEmail: During the pilot, the team is reachable through the project's GitHub page.
contact.medical: We cannot answer medical questions here. Ask your pharmacist in the app (Questions), or contact your doctor. In an emergency, call 999.

pharmacists.title: For pharmacists and doctors
pharmacists.intro: OushodhSathi needs registered pharmacists and doctors to confirm or dismiss what the rules find. Every finding is decided by a person, with their name and registration number on it.

p: A keyboard-driven queue, red findings first. Each finding shows the strip photos, brands, generics, the rule that fired and its source. Most take under a minute.

You can add what each medicine is for, approve the times of day, confirm allergies and answer family questions. You never need to tell a family to stop a medicine; that stays between the patient and their doctor.

Contact us with your name, whether you are a pharmacist or a doctor, and your Pharmacy Council or BMDC registration number. We send you a personal invite link; you can stop at any time and your login is revoked.
